# Chapter 01: Toolchain, types and errors

<!-- README generated by Claude from my code. The code in this folder is my own. -->

## Programs

| Program | Run it | Practices |
|---------|--------|-----------|
| [`practice/`](practice/main.go) | `go run ./ch01-toolchain-types-errors/practice` | multiple return values, `(value, error)` pattern, `errors.New`, wrapping with `fmt.Errorf("%w")`, `strconv.Atoi`, `:=` vs `=` |

### Functions in `practice/main.go`

| Function | What it does | Concept |
|----------|--------------|---------|
| `divide(a, b float64)` | returns an error instead of dividing by zero | returning an `error` instead of throwing |
| `half(n int)` | rejects odd numbers | guard clause + early `return` |
| `doubleIt(s string)` | parses a string and doubles it | wrapping a library error with `%w` |

`main` has commented-out experiments with `:=` redeclaration and `var n int = nil`, which I kept as a record of what does and doesn't compile.

## Concepts covered
- The `go` toolchain: `go mod init`, `go run`, `go vet`, `gofmt`
- Packages, `package main`, exported vs unexported names
- Zero values, and why `nil` isn't valid for an `int`
- `var` vs `:=`, and the "at least one new variable" rule for `:=`
- Multiple return values and the `if err != nil` pattern
